c1-oba-0001: Obadiah warns Edom that its own allies will turn against it. Let's read Obadiah 1:7.
c2-oba-0001: Obadiah lists what Edom should not have done in Judah's day of distress. Let's look at Obadiah 1:12 and 14 together.
c2-num-0011: Edom's king refused Israel passage and came out to bar the way. Let's read Numbers 20:17 and 19.
c3-num-0005: Edom refused Israel passage through his territory, and came out against them with many men. Let's turn to Numbers 20:20 and 21.
c3-oba-0001: Obadiah says Edom will be made small, and he remembers the day strangers carried Judah's forces captive. Let's read Obadiah 1:2 and 11.
c3-oba-0002: The LORD will destroy the wise men from Edom, and then Obadiah turns to the house of Jacob. Let's open Obadiah 1:8 and 17.
c3-oba-0003: Obadiah condemns Edom for violence against its brother Jacob, then pictures Jacob as a fire and Joseph as a flame. Let's read Obadiah 1:10 and 18.
c3-gen-0012: The LORD told Rebekah that two nations were in her womb. Later Genesis records the kings who reigned in Esau's line. Let's read Genesis 25:23 and 36:33.
c1-nah-0001: Amid Nahum's warnings of judgment on Nineveh, he pauses to call the LORD good, a shelter when trouble comes. Let's read Nahum 1:7.
c2-nah-0001: The LORD promises Judah that He will break the yoke off them, and then a messenger of good tidings appears on the mountains. Let's look at Nahum 1:13 and 15 together.
c2-nah-0002: Nahum compares Nineveh with another great city that had waters around her, and Ethiopia and Egypt as her strength. Let's read Nahum 3:8 and 9.
c3-jon-0001: God saw that Nineveh turned from its evil way and relented, and when word reached the king, he laid aside his robe and covered himself with sackcloth. Let's turn to Jonah 3:6 and 10.
c3-nah-0001: With an overflowing flood the LORD will make an utter end there, and later Nahum describes the palace being dissolved. Let's read Nahum 1:8 and 2:6.
c3-nah-0002: Nahum says affliction will not rise up a second time, and the closing verse speaks of Nineveh's injury. Let's check Nahum 1:9 and 3:19.
c3-nah-0003: Nahum mocks Nineveh: "Man the fort! Watch the road!" Later the city is told to draw water for the siege and fortify its strongholds. Let's read Nahum 2:1 and 3:14.
c3-jon-0002: God relented from the disaster He had said He would bring on Nineveh, and later asks whether He should not pity that great city. Let's dig into Jonah 3:10 and 4:11.
c1-zep-0001: Zephaniah announces judgment on Judah for mixed worship: people swear oaths by the LORD, and also by another. Let's read Zephaniah 1:5.
c2-zep-0001: The LORD will search Jerusalem closely and punish the men who say He will do neither good nor evil. Let's open Zephaniah 1:12 and 13.
c2-zep-0002: Zephaniah calls the humble of the land to seek the LORD, righteousness, and humility before His anger comes. Let's read Zephaniah 2:2 and 3.
c3-zep-0001: Zephaniah says Jerusalem's priests have polluted the sanctuary, and her judges are evening wolves. Let's look closely at Zephaniah 3:3 and 4.
c3-zep-0002: Zephaniah condemns those who have turned back from following the LORD, yet he also shows the Mighty One in your midst, who will save. Let's read Zephaniah 1:6 and 3:17.
c3-zep-0003: Zephaniah calls the undesirable nation to gather itself together, and later the LORD tells the faithful to wait for Him. Let's turn to Zephaniah 2:1 and 3:8.
c3-zep-0004: Zephaniah pronounces woe on the oppressing city, and earlier pictures Nineveh dwelling securely and speaking in her heart. Let's read Zephaniah 2:15 and 3:1.
c3-zep-0005: The LORD stretches out His hand against Judah, and later Nineveh is left a desolation. Let's read Zephaniah 1:4 and 2:14.
c1-phm-0001: Paul's letter is addressed to Philemon, and he names others as well. Let's read Philemon 1:2.
c2-phm-0001: Paul thanks God for Philemon in his prayers. Let's look at Philemon 1:4 and 5 together.
c2-col-0004: Paul says Tychicus is coming, and Onesimus is traveling with him. Let's read Colossians 4:7 and 9.
c3-phm-0001: Paul says he might be bold enough to command Philemon, yet he wants to do nothing without Philemon's consent. Let's check Philemon 1:8 and 14.
c3-phm-0002: Paul prays that the sharing of Philemon's faith may become effective, and he writes with confidence in Philemon's obedience. Let's read Philemon 1:6 and 21.
c3-phm-0003: Paul suggests Onesimus departed for a while so Philemon might have him back forever. Let's dig into Philemon 1:15 and 18.
c3-phm-0004: Paul calls himself a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and he admits he wished to keep Onesimus with him on Philemon's behalf. Let's read Philemon 1:1 and 13.
c3-phm-0005: Paul rejoices that Philemon has refreshed others, and now he is sending Onesimus back. Let's go to Philemon 1:4 and 12.
c1-2jn-0001: The Elder writes to the elect lady and rejoices greatly to have found certain people walking in truth. Let's read Second John 1:4.
c2-2jn-0001: The Elder reminds the lady that what he writes is nothing new, and then he explains what love is. Let's look closely at Second John 1:2 and 6.
c2-2jn-0002: The Elder writes about a visitor who does not bring the doctrine of Christ. Let's read Second John 1:10 and 11.
c3-2jn-0001: The Elder tells his readers to look to themselves so they do not lose what was worked for. Let's turn to Second John 1:8 and 11.
c3-2jn-0002: The Elder contrasts those who abide in the doctrine of Christ with those who do not, and his greeting names the Lord Jesus Christ. Let's read Second John 1:3 and 9.
c3-2jn-0003: The elect sister's household sends greetings, and earlier the Elder warns of many deceivers who have gone out. Let's check Second John 1:13 and 7.
c1-3jn-0001: The Elder wrote, but one man would not welcome him, and that man loves to have the preeminence among them. Let's read Third John 1:9.
c2-3jn-0001: The Elder says we ought to welcome such workers, then describes a man who resists him, turns the brethren away, and forbids those who wish to welcome them. Let's read Third John 1:8 and 10.
c2-3jn-0002: Gaius has been faithful to brethren and to strangers, who have borne witness of his love. Let's go to Third John 1:5 and 6.
c3-3jn-0001: The Elder urges Gaius to imitate the good, not the evil, and then commends a man everyone speaks well of, adding his own witness. Let's read Third John 1:11 and 12.
c3-3jn-0002: The Elder has no greater joy than hearing that those he taught walk in truth, and then he explains why the traveling brethren set out. Let's look at Third John 1:4 and 7 together.
c3-3jn-0003: The Elder urges Gaius to imitate the good, then says he has many things to write, but does not wish to write them in the usual way. Let's open Third John 1:11 and 13.
c2-exo-0022: At Sinai the LORD sent Moses to tell Israel what they would be to Him if they kept His covenant. Let's read Exodus 19:6.
c2-2sa-0009: God promises David's offspring, "he shall be My son." If he commits iniquity, the LORD will chasten him. Let's read Second Samuel 7:14 and 15.
c3-jer-0013: Jeremiah says the new covenant will not be like the one made when the LORD took their fathers by the hand to lead them from Egypt, which they broke. Let's turn to Jeremiah 31:32 and 34.
c3-heb-0009: Hebrews explains why a second covenant was needed, and then quotes Jeremiah's promise. Let's read Hebrews 8:7 and 8.
c3-2sa-0009: God reminds David that He has been with him and has cut off those who opposed him, and then He promises to plant His people. Let's dig into Second Samuel 7:9 and 10.
c3-gen-0013: The LORD makes a covenant with Abram about the land, and earlier He named a sign of His covenant with Noah and every living creature. Let's read Genesis 9:12 and 15:18.
c3-gen-0014: God says the waters shall never again become a flood, and later He tells Abram what he shall be under the covenant. Let's look closely at Genesis 9:15 and 17:4.
c3-gen-0015: The LORD appears to Abram and calls him to walk before Him, and earlier He reminds Abram that He brought him out so he might be given this land. Let's read Genesis 15:7 and 17:1.
c3-gen-0016: God names the creatures included in His covenant with Noah, and later Abram waits beside the divided sacrifice. Let's go to Genesis 9:10 and 15:11.
c3-gen-0017: Abram asks how he will know that he will inherit the land, and later God says He will make His covenant between Himself and Abram, and He adds another promise. Let's read Genesis 15:8 and 17:2.
